A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of IRT in the study of adolescent alcohol use and related problems can be a valuable approach for researchers to use.

the use of IRT to measure adolescent drinking problems provides a more accurate assessment of the underlying construct of drinking problems than traditional approaches, and that this improved measurement leads to stronger and more stable prospective associations between adolescent drinking problems and later drinking and other psychiatric disorders.

the use of IRT methods in the measurement of alcohol problems in adolescence can be useful for the following reasons: (1) IRT methods can be used to improve the measurement properties of the AUDIT‐C, which is a widely used and valid measure of alcohol problems in adults; and (2) IRT‐based scores can be used to identify individuals who have alcohol problems in adolescence, who may benefit from early intervention.
